newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates barely higher in week - Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates barely higher in week - Freddie Mac.

text.p: Home mortgage rates edged higher this week, as the Federal Reserve decided to hold interest rates steady, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.92 percent, up from 7.91 percent last week, while 15-year mortgage rates rose to 7.45 percent from 7.44 percent.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates rose to 5.80 percent from 5.78 percent last week, Freddie Mac said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.01 percent, the 15-year 7.51 percent and the adjustable rate 5.75 percent.
"The Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates stable will promote a continuance of the affordable mortgage market we are enjoying now," said Freddie Mac deputy chief economist Frank Nothaft.
"Housing activity continues to be brisk, as shown by the 2.6 percent increase in housing starts in April, and the housing market will remain active at least through the spring," Nothaft added.
The Federal Open Market Committee decided on Tuesday to leave interest rates unchanged.

Last week the Commerce Department said housing starts rose 2.6 percent in April to a 1.473 million unit annual rate, while the Labour Department reported that consumer prices rose only 0.1 percent last month.
Next Tuesday the National Association of Realtors will issue April existing home sales data.

Lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30-year mortgages, up from 1.6 percent last week. They charged 1.6 percent on 15-year loans, unchanged from the prior week, and 1.5 percent on ARM loans, up from 1.4 percent last week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
